description:
AMD just took a $1 billion charge to secure AI chips for OpenAI and Meta. We’re breaking down what this massive hardware bill means for the future of your favorite AI tools.

Alex, Jamie, and Rufus debate the biggest artificial intelligence news from the last 24–48 hours, with three distinct stories, competing perspectives and practical takeaways.

What we covered:
• AMD faces $1 billion quarterly charge from OpenAI and Meta AI chip supply agreements
• Anthropic adds text watermark information in platform release notes
• NVIDIA says AI agents and digital twins are speeding semiconductor fab work

What changed. Who wins. What you do next.

The Edge: what changed, who wins, who is exposed, and what to watch next.

Listener question: When you hear about a 'billion-dollar' AI cost, does it make you feel the tech is more serious or more risky?

title_candidates_v3_3.listener_promise: By the end, you'll understand the massive hardware costs behind AI, the new security risks to your sessions, and how AI is trying to speed up its own production.

positions.alex: Believes we are in a 'growing pains' phase where we must build the tools to manage the agents we've unleashed.
positions.jamie: Argues that until systems are legible and secure to the people they affect, these 'infrastructure' and 'safety' launches are just new ways to hide risk.
positions.rufus: Observes that the market is currently paying for the 'infrastructure of control' because it's the only way to keep the AI boom going without a catastrophic failure.

concession.gives_ground_on: Admits that token-stealing malware makes the 'growing pains' argument feel much more urgent and personal.

title_candidates_v3_3.who_is_exposed: The average user who relies on AI tools without understanding the risks of session token theft.
title_candidates_v3_3.normal_person_payoff: Check your device security and be aware that password resets aren't a universal fix for AI account security.
